2607.25425.title: The Disruptive Impact of Large Language Models on Capture the Flag Competitions and the Path Toward Fair Play
2607.25425.paper_summary: Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions are among cybersecurity's most effective training grounds, developing practical skill across cryptography, web exploitation, and binary exploitation. Large language models (LLMs) can now solve a growing share of challenges with minimal human input, raising urgent questions about fairness, the validity of rankings, and whether participation still delivers the learning that justifies the effort. This paper reports a mixed-methods study of LLM impact on modern CTFs, combining a synthesis of published benchmarks, including a recent government evaluation, case studies of live competition across three challenge categories, structured observation of the public channels where the community debates AI use, and semi-structured interviews with experienced players and organisers. We map the current human-machine capability boundary by category, showing that easy and intermediate challenges in cryptography, web, and binary exploitation are now reliably automated while narrower sub-categories continue to resist. We find that community disagreement about whether AI should be permitted is downstream of an undeclared prior question: what a competition is for. Against this backdrop we contribute a four-component safeguard framework, combining tiered competition divisions, LLM-resistant challenge design, telemetry used investigatively, and a draft community code of conduct, together with a decision tool that ties the combination of safeguards to a competition's declared purpose. The argument reaches beyond CTFs to any setting in cybersecurity where a demonstrated result is taken as evidence of an underlying ability.
2607.25425.paper_summary_zh: Capture the Flag (CTF) 競賽是網路安全領域中最有效的訓練場之一，培養在密碼學、網路利用和二進位利用方面的實用技能。大型語言模型 (LLMs) 現在能夠以最小的人力輸入解決越來越多的挑戰，這引發了關於公平性、排名有效性以及參與是否仍然能夠提供正當努力的學習的緊迫問題。本文報告了一項關於 LLM 對現代 CTF 影響的混合方法研究，結合了已發表基準的綜合，包括最近的政府評估、三個挑戰類別的現場競賽案例研究、對社區討論 AI 使用的公共頻道的結構性觀察，以及與經驗豐富的玩家和組織者的半結構化訪談。我們按類別映射當前的人機能力邊界，顯示密碼學、網路和二進位利用中的簡單和中等挑戰現在已經可靠地自動化，而較狹窄的子類別仍然抵抗。我們發現，社區對於是否應該允許 AI 的分歧是未宣告的先前問題的下游：競賽的目的為何。在這種背景下，我們提出了一個四組件的保障框架，結合了分級競賽部門、抗 LLM 的挑戰設計、用於調查的遙測，以及草擬的社區行為準則，還有一個將保障組合與競賽的宣告目的聯繫起來的決策工具。這一論點超越了 CTF，適用於任何在網路安全領域中，經過驗證的結果被視為潛在能力的證據的情境。
